original_question: Let T be the 2-dimensional torus. A homeomorphism h: T -> T is called simple if it is supported on an embedded open disc, and the disc norm of h is the least number of simple homeomorphisms whose composition equals h. Do there exist homeomorphisms of T with arbitrarily large disc norm?
target_in_paper: Section 13, open problem “Homeomorphism of the torus”: “Is there a homeomorphism of the 2-dimensional torus with arbitrarily large disc norm?”
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s actual formulation in Section 13. It correctly identifies the ambient manifold as the 2-dimensional torus, uses the paper’s notion of a simple homeomorphism as one supported on an embedded open disc, and asks exactly the paper’s unboundedness question for the disc norm. It also does not add extra assumptions (such as smoothness, orientation-preservation, or isotopy-to-the-identity) that the paper does not impose.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, spell out “supported on an embedded open disc” as: there exists an embedded open disc D ⊂ T^2 such that h|_{T^2 \setminus D} = id.
State the disc norm as the minimum n ∈ N such that h = h1 ∘ ··· ∘ hn with each hi simple.
Unpack “arbitrarily large” into an explicit quantifier: for every N ∈ N, there exists h ∈ Homeo(T^2) with disc norm at least N.
Use T^2 (or explicitly “the 2-dimensional torus”) rather than a bare symbol T if you want the question to be fully self-contained without prior notation.
refined_question: Let T^2 be the 2-dimensional torus. Call a homeomorphism h ∈ Homeo(T^2) simple if there exists an embedded open disc D ⊂ T^2 such that h|_{T^2 \setminus D} = id. Define the disc norm of h to be the least integer n such that h can be written as h = h1 ∘ ··· ∘ hn with each hi simple. Is it true that for every N ∈ N there exists a homeomorphism h : T^2 → T^2 whose disc norm is at least N?
justification: The relevant target is not a conjecture or theorem but the open problem in Section 13 of the paper. The paper gives the definitions of “simple” homeomorphism and “disc norm” immediately before posing the torus question, and your draft already tracks that wording very closely. The only real refinements needed are to make the support condition explicit, to write the factorization defining the norm explicitly, and to replace the informal phrase “arbitrarily large” by its quantifier form “for every N ∈ N.” The paper does not provide a separate proved equivalent reformulation nearby, so the faithful rewrite should stay with this exact unboundedness question and not broaden it.
